The amount of machinery, equipment and tools needed to turn these materials into the parts needed for a car are very high and expensive. You can't just take these raw materials and build your own car in your garage for less than $20K.

There are so many other costs; labor, engineering, design, marketing, administration, which all add to the final costs.

The expertise in many disciplines adds extra cost to the auto making process. The engineering alone for a new car is a big expense because it needs to be done on many different levels and disciplines by people who are educated in those fields. They need to be paid for their knowledge and expertise. Same with the designers, machinists, fabricators, laborers and all the support staff needed to run a factory filled with these types of workers.

That’s why the more cars you make of the same model the less these “other” costs are per car.

Yes, this is how economies of scale work. The investment in the tools, equipment, professional service, labor and materials gets offset by the number of salable vehicles the factory can produce. A $1.5 million body panel molding machine spreads its cost out over many vehicles it makes parts for thereby paying for itself over time (minus the ongoing maintenance and repair costs it will inevitably incur). Same with all the other capital investments for the factory, including the very building where it all takes place. You must produce and sell enough vehicles at a specific price in order to keep the whole thing going and the workers employed. This is how manufacturing under a capitalistic system works.
